title: How Training Tendons Makes Your Punch Heavier
description:
A heavy punch is not a strong arm. It is a stiff wrist and a springy forearm tendon delivering the force your body already made. Learn the chain, then train it.

Educational content, not medical advice. Stop if you feel pain.

#punch #boxing #tendon #calisthenics #strength

scenes.caption: SHADOWBOX ONCE
scenes.narration: Shadowbox one punch in the air, right now. Feel it. Did your fist snap, or did it flop? A snapping punch and a floppy punch can come from the same arm, the same muscles, the same person. The difference is not strength. It is what happens at the very end of the chain, in your wrist, in the last ten centimetres before impact.

scenes.title: THE PUNCH CHAIN
layers: delivers the force - or leaks it
scenes.narration: A punch is a chain. Your legs and hips make the force. Your core transfers it. And your wrist tendon delivers it. If that last link is soft, force leaks out at the wrist, your hand bends, and the punch lands soft no matter how strong you are. If the last link is stiff, the whole force arrives in one snap. Fighters have known this forever. They just call it a heavy hand.

scenes.label: DECIDES THE WHOLE PUNCH
scenes.sub: the wrist is the shortest link - and the weakest one
scenes.narration: Ten centimetres. That is all the wrist is. The shortest link in the chain, and the one almost nobody trains on purpose. Push-up handles, knuckle push-ups, wrist rollers, all of it is tendon work disguised as old-school training. Today we do the modern version, with a timer, together.
Move one. Grip squeeze hold. Squeeze anything hard, a ball, a towel, your own fist, and hold it still. Thirty seconds. The forearm tendons are loading. Go.
Move two. Dead hang. Straight arms, still body. The hang loads your wrist and finger tendons under your whole bodyweight, the exact load a punch asks them to survive. Go.

scenes.caption: THE WRIST TEST
scenes.narration: Here is a test for the wrist itself. Hold your arm out straight and flick your hand down and up, fast, like you are shaking water off it. Now do it again, but keep your wrist locked stiff the whole time. Feel the difference? A loose wrist wobbles and wastes the motion. A stiff wrist moves as one piece with the forearm. That stiffness is not bone. It is tendon tone, and it is trainable, the same way we trained the Achilles and the fingers.

scenes.head: OLD SCHOOL - ALREADY KNEW THIS
lines: every old gym trained the wrist
without ever saying the word tendon.
scenes.foot: The science caught up with the old gym
scenes.narration: And here is the funny part. The old gyms already knew all of this. Knuckle push-ups, wrist rollers, heavy bag rounds, rope climbs. Every one of those loads the wrist tendon under force, and nobody in those gyms ever said the word tendon. They said heavy hands, snap, and bone density. The science has finally caught up with the old gym, and it says the same thing: the wrist is trained by loading it, slowly, heavily, and often.

scenes.caption: THE RULE OF THE WRIST
scenes.narration: One rule before you train it. Never punch a hard surface with a loose wrist. Every injury story in boxing starts the same way, a beginner hitting the bag hard with a wrist that was never trained, bending on impact. The circuit we are doing builds the stiffness first, with holds and hangs, and only then do you hit things. Build the cable, then use the cable. That order is the whole sport.

scenes.label: THE HONEST TIMELINE
scenes.sub: a stiff wrist is a trained tendon - built slowly, kept for years
scenes.narration: Ninety days of this, three times a week, and your wrist stops being the weak link. Shadowbox again in ninety days and feel the snap. Tell me in the comments if your punch feels heavier. Next video, we feed the tendon: the collagen protocol, what to eat and when. This is Wire Strength. Train the cable.
